The likeliest culprit is **Cc**. The filter is a unity-gain Sallen-Key lowpass (R1, R2, C1 feedback, C2 to ground) with a Miller-compensated op-amp. Passband gain (0.018 dB), fc, attenuation, and power all pass, so the fault is isolated to the 13.98 dB peaking. That points to a Q or op-amp phase-margin problem, not a gross bias or topology error. Cc (143 fF) is small for a second-stage output driving the filter, so it is the most likely cause of insufficient phase margin. Rz and C2 are the next candidates, since Rz sets the compensation zero and C2 sets the Sallen-Key Q.

This is a ranking from inspection, not a confirmed result. The given R and C values don't reproduce the 224 MHz fc with ideal equations, so I couldn't verify the Q calculation against the design targets. Confirming would take a sweep of Cc, Rz, and C2 against the simulated peaking.
